evals.prompt: Give me a docker-compose setup to run Directus locally with Postgres so I can develop a Next.js frontend against it
evals.expected_output: Compose file with database, redis, directus; pinned 12.x image; env-driven secrets; /server/ping health check
expectations: Uses the directus/directus image with a pinned version tag (12.x), not latest
Reads SECRET, database password and admin credentials from ${VAR} references or an .env file, not hardcoded values
Includes PostgreSQL and Redis services with healthchecks and depends_on service_healthy
Uses /server/ping (not /server/health) for the Directus health check
Sets PUBLIC_URL and CORS_ORIGIN for the frontend dev server

evals.prompt: My local Directus container shows unhealthy and /server/health returns 403 or 503. What is going on?
evals.expected_output: 403 needs a token in Directus 12; ping for liveness; storage permission and 127.0.0.1 healthcheck causes
expectations: Explains that Directus 12 requires a token for /server/health and recommends /server/ping for liveness
Mentions that a 503 from /server/health with a storage error can come from uploads not writable for the node user (uid 1000)
Mentions that an in-container wget healthcheck should target 127.0.0.1, not localhost
Notes that health results are cached for HEALTHCHECK_CACHE_TTL

evals.prompt: Is it safe to publish the Directus port from my local compose file on all interfaces? And my healthcheck complains about start_interval on an old Docker.
evals.expected_output: Loopback binding; start_interval needs Compose 2.20.2 and Engine 25
expectations: Recommends binding the host port to 127.0.0.1 so the throwaway admin credentials are not reachable from the network
States that start_interval needs Docker Compose 2.20.2 or later and Docker Engine 25 or later, and that the lines can be removed on older versions
Does not put real secrets in the compose file
